name: Ciclosporin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

key_interactions.drug_or_class: NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, vancomycin, amphotericin B, co-trimoxazole, ciprofloxacin, tacrolimus, fibrates, colchicine and other drugs that impair kidney function
key_interactions.effect: Additive kidney impairment, especially with dehydration (label).
key_interactions.action: Monitor serum creatinine closely; reduce a dose or change treatment if kidney function falls.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: CYP3A4 or P-gp inhibitors that raise cyclosporine (diltiazem, verapamil, nicardipine, fluconazole, itraconazole, ketoconazole, voriconazole, azithromycin, clarithromycin, erythromycin, methylprednisolone, allopurinol, amiodarone, colchicine, metoclopramide, HIV protease inhibitors)
key_interactions.action: Monitor cyclosporine blood levels and adjust the dose.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Inducers that lower cyclosporine (rifampin, rifabutin, carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, nafcillin, octreotide, terbinafine, ticlopidine)
key_interactions.action: Monitor cyclosporine blood levels and adjust the dose.

key_interactions.effect: St John's wort can cause subtherapeutic levels and graft loss; grapefruit raises levels (label).
Severe digitalis toxicity within days of starting cyclosporine (label).
Higher colchicine levels; myopathy and neuropathy, especially with kidney impairment (label).
key_interactions.action: Reduce the colchicine dose and monitor.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Statins, aliskiren, dabigatran, repaglinide, sirolimus, prednisolone
key_interactions.action: See the other drug's label for dose limits; monitor for toxicity.
